messages.subject: new user question
parts:
Hello I am a new user of nimble, and I am troubleshooting a model that runs in jags.  The model code is attached.  If I run the following code in nimble I get estimates of phi, psi, pd_a and pd_b, gamma1 and gamma2.

simple.model <- nimbleModel(code=nimble.fixed.s, constants=constants, data=jags.onestate.data, inits=inits, check = FALSE)
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(simple.model)
Cmodel <- compileNimble(simple.model)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = simple.model)
Cmcmc$run(10000)
samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)

However if I run this code 
ms<-nimbleMCMC(simple.model, data = jags.onestate.data, inits = inits,
               monitors = c("pd_a", "psi", "phi"), thin = 10,
               niter = 10000, nburnin = 5000, nchains = 3,
               summary = TRUE, WAIC = FALSE)

I get an error
problem initializing stochastic node y[1582, 2, 15]: logProb is -Inf

Ideas on what I'm doing wrong?

Thanks,

Robin

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: new user question
parts:
Interesting, indeed, Robin.  We're keen to help, but we'd need a reproducible example to really investigate what's going on.

Without any more information, I would guess that one of the "parent" nodes of the "y[1582, 2, 15]" node is not properly initialized, and for reasons I can't guess.  Further, NIMBLE is unable to initialize it using it's regular initialization routine -- which is good; but can't fix everything.

Are you ok to send a reproducible example?  Either on- or off-list?  That would require the variables you used:

nimble.fixed.s
constants
jags.onestate.data
inits

Cheers!
Daniel

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: new user question
parts:
If you're simply trying to have nimbleMCMC accomplish the same steps as the more explicit nimbleModel-buildMCMC-compileNimble-Cmcmc$run sequence that you did get to work, I think you need the first argument to nimbleMCMC to be nimble.fixed.s and also to include the same constants = constants argument you used for nimbleModel.  Alternatively it should work to give constants = c(constants, jags.onestate.data) and omit the data argument.

nimbleMCMC just manages the sequence of steps you've already done with some helpful management of chains and output.  You can get that management from the steps you did but with runMCMC(Cmcmc, <look at other arguments>) instead of Cmcmc$run().

Alternatively you can give nimbleMCMC "model = simple.model" and omit the constants, data, and inits, since they were provided when you created simple.model.  However, if you've already compiled simple.model from the first workflow, then you'll need to re-create simple.model for nimbleMCMC, so you might as well pass the code, constants, data and inits and let nimbleMCMC create the model.

nimbleMCMC will use check=TRUE by default, which can be slow can generate warnings or show messages about incomplete initialization.  If you want the same behavior are your direct use of nimbleModel, use check=FALSE again.  The first workflow always provides more control.
